response.text: Accrual accounting records income and expenses when they happen, not when money changes hands. If you make a sale today but the customer pays next month, accrual records the sale now. If you receive a bill today but pay it later, accrual records the cost now. Cash-basis accounting waits until cash is actually received or paid. That can make results jumpy: a month with many payments looks great, and a month of big bills can look bad even if business is steady. Accrual gives a clearer view of ongoing performance because it matches what you earned with the costs to earn it. Cash-basis is simpler and can work for very small operations. In short: accrual shows the business’s true activity over time; cash-basis shows the actual cash moving in and out right now.
